question: Will the European Council reach a political agreement on the overall 2028-2034 Multiannual Financial Framework before January 1, 2027?

calls.reasoning: Base rate: in recent MFF cycles (2005, 2012-13, 2020) the first leaders' summit with figures failed and the targeted deadline slipped, with deals coming 3-6 months later. This cycle the second attempt (Dec 17-18) is only 3 weeks after the Nov 26-27 special summit. Strong forcing deadline: Macron says no political room after December because of the April 2027 French election, and Costa warns that missing December means no deal until about October 2027. Against: Costa's Nov 21 box (about 1.78T, -204bn) was rejected as 'not a basis' by France and the Dutch/Swedish governments, and only called a 'first step' by Merz; frugals want hundreds of billions more in cuts while 17 Friends of Cohesion resist; Merz's Ukraine linkage has drawn veto threats from Fico, Babis and others. Deadline pressure lifts the odds above the slip base rate, but the gaps are wide with unanimity required. No prediction market found on Polymarket, Manifold, Kalshi or bookmakers.

calls.reasoning: Base rate: in recent MFF cycles (2005, 2012-13, 2020) the first leaders' summit aimed at a deal failed and agreement came at a later summit 3-6 months on; here the follow-up (17-18 Dec) is only ~3 weeks after the 26-27 Nov special summit, and a deal would come ~17 months after the July 2025 proposal, faster than any recent precedent. Current evidence: Costa's 21 Nov box (~10% cut) was rejected by Germany, the other frugals, France, the cohesion group and the Eastern tax opponents; Slovakia threatens a veto, Hungary is a blocking risk, the EP calls it no basis for consent; ambassadors failed to agree; diplomats expect the November summit to mandate more work and call a year-end deal unlikely; Meloni and Kristersson openly doubt the deadline. Upward pull: strong deadline pressure (Costa warns of slippage to Oct 2027 because of 2027 elections incl. France; Macron says no room after January), reported Merz-Macron convergence on own resources, and the possibility of a marathon December summit. No prediction market found.

calls.reasoning: Past rounds: the first leaders' summit with figures failed in both Nov 2012 and Feb 2020, and deals came 3-5 months later; here a deal would need to land at the 17-18 Dec summit only three weeks after the 26-27 Nov special summit. Costa's 21 Nov proposal (EUR 1.582tn) was rejected by France, the frugals (Merz: too big), the V4 plus Austria (Magyar: not a basis) and the Parliament. Strong push the other way: the French election on 18 Apr 2027, with Le Pen favourite, gives everyone a reason to close in December (Macron: no room after January), and Agence Europe reports the EU27 largely convinced they must finish by year-end. Against that, Sweden and Meloni doubt the deadline, and October's conclusions softened it to 'timely agreement'. No prediction market found on Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold.
